newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes slightly lower, market drifts.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes slightly lower, market drifts.

text.p: Gold prices were less than a dollar under Friday's close on Monday morning reflecting the market's lack of direction following a lustreless option expiry on Comex, dealers said.
Established ranges should hold without too much stress although platinum might weaken slightly now that tensions from Russian supply issues have largely been absorbed, they said.
Gold fixed at $352.05 per ounce down just 85 cents from Friday afternoon's fixing and against a $352.50/$353.00 close.
Prices were forecast to drift after interest was light in the Far East following through from a $1.50 lower close on the Comex April contract at $352.90.
"The range is still $350-$355 and gold should not see enough pressure to put it under $350," one analyst said.
Above the market, producer selling has been seen at $353.00 and heavier selling was booked in at $354.00 and over.
There was no producer business noted eaerly on Monday, according to dealers contacted by Reuters.
Meanwhile, physical demand has eased in Europe since the dollar began its climb against other currencies.
"They have their gold investments now and that's it,"one dealer said.
Gold was forecast for a $350.50-$353.00 range today and a softer dollar against the yen and mark helped keep gold steady in light early business, dealers said.
Silver was forecast for a 10-cent bracket between $5.20-$5.30 after attempts to penetrate the top of that range were turned back three times last week.
A golden cross between the 50-day and 200-day moving averages last week brought in light fund buying on Thursday but there was no follow through, they said.
"Silver has had a problem at $5.30 for some time now," one analyst said.
After correcting from its February high of around $406.00 some further weakness was possible in platinum, analysts said.
"A bit more could be expected on the downside now that the Russia supply issue is less of a concern," one analyst said.

There was still no sign of talks beginning between Russia's export negotiators and the Japanese trade houses on 1997 supply contracts after officials in Moscow last week forecast the first 1997 exports moving by the end of March.
Platinum was at $380.75/$381.75 and palladium unchanged at $152.00/$153.00.
